messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT opened — high p99 latency observed in eu-west-1/gpu-pool-2, automated alert threshold tripped :rotating_light:
emily: i got paged, looking now. any deploys around the window?
raj: yup, rolling 2026-03-17T22:05 UTC -> quantize-path V2 enabled to 20% canary (flag: feature/quant-route-v2). p99 token latency jumped from ~180ms -> ~1s on some slices. throughput dropped.
mike: logs show kernel selector falling back to 'fallback_linear' with lots of small microbatches, KV cache hits down 40%.
julia: confirmed 20% canary targeted eu-west-1 pools, we expected safe but saw sawtooth latency pattern.
sam: can we flip the kill-switch on the flag? want to stop rollout before wider impact.
emily: agreed. flipping flag for quant-route-v2 -> OFF for eu-west-1. will run quick smoke.
ops-bot: runbook step: toggle feature flag via /ops/flags service, curl below:
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.internal.redwood/flags/quant-route-v2/toggle" -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","state":"off"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```
raj: doing the toggle now.
raj: toggled -> API returned 200, rollout aborted.
oncall-bot: FLAG_CHANGE applied by raj at 5801234578 (quant-route-v2 -> OFF for eu-west-1).
emily: watching metrics... p50 normalizing, p99 dropping. KV hit rate recovering.
mike: batching window returned to ~32ms from 8ms, microbatch counts down. kernel selector stable on 'fast_attn_v3' again.
julia: customer impact: three enterprise tenants in eu-west-1 saw elevated latencies and some request timeouts for 12 minutes. no broad data loss.
sam: opening short bridge for postmortem/impact comms, adding infra and product.
emily: mitigation done — rollback of feature flag. recommend full rollback of canary release and stop any further rolls until root cause.
ops-bot: incident severity S2 -> customer-facing notice required? product says yes for affected customers.
raj: quick root cause notes: quant-route-v2 changes altered kernel selection heuristics for short sequences, causing more kernels to select fallback path under medium load; combined with canary hitting a hot pool led to KV cache churn.
emily: next steps: 1) keep flag off globally for 1 hour 2) run synthetic perf tests against quant-route-v2 on isolated pool 3) plan rollback or patch of kernel heuristic 4) customer outreach draft (product).
mike: I'll capture traces for the affected time window and dump kernel selection debug logs to /tmp/incident-5801234567.tar.gz and share.
julia: i'll coordinate with product for comms, need list of affected tenants and MRR impact.
sam: handing off to oncall SRE rotation (raj) for monitoring and follow-up. i'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow.
emily: thanks team — close this thread when postmortem invites sent. :thumbsup:
